title: SignalForge SDK: auth, KMS & sandbox quickstart lab
summary: AE + SE walked SignalForge engineering through Redwood SDK quickstart (py/ts), auth patterns (API keys, GCP Workload Identity), sandbox provisioning, and KMS integration. Covered hosting options, VPC/KMS, basic performance tuning (batching/quant), and next steps for a 2-week pilot and security questionnaire. Some transcript noise/mis-recognitions (product names and acronyms).
topics: Auth methods: API keys, GCP Workload Identity, SAML/SSO notes
Dev->Prod migration: Dedicated vs Hosted vs Private (VPC)
Optimize: batching, KV cache, quantization suggestions
action_items: Ava Martinez: Share sandbox invitation link + quickstart repo (py/ts) and sample env vars; due 2025-04-03
Liam Chen: Provide short benchmark sheet template (latency/cost) and recommended model/quant profiles for SignalForge use case; due 2025-04-06
SignalForge / Nora Patel: Complete security questionnaire and send to Priya; due 2025-04-08
Samir Khan (SignalForge): Confirm KMS provider and whether HSM required; due 2025-04-07
next_steps: Start 2-week pilot on Redwood hosted sandbox - Redwood to provision sandbox and keys
Redwood to run small benchmark with SignalForge test prompt set and share results
Schedule technical deep dive (private deployment options) if security review passes
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-04-02
Time: 14:30 PT
Duration: 58 mins
Attendees: Ava Martinez, Liam Chen, Priya Rao - Redwood; Nora Patel, Diego Ramos, Eli Zhao, Samir Khan - SignalForge

[00:00] Ava Martinez: Hey everybody thanks for hopping on. I'm Ava from Redwood Inference, AE. Joining me is Liam Chen our SE and Priya from DevEx. How's everyone doing?
[00:12] Nora Patel: Good thanks, excited to see the quickstart. We've got a pretty tight timeline - want to try the SDK in our staging this week if possible.
[00:20] Ava Martinez: Great, that's what we planned for today - a live walkthrough of the Python and TypeScript SDK quickstart, auth options, and then a short demo of KMS integration and sandbox provisioning. We'll leave time for questions.
[00:34] Liam Chen: Quick note, I'll be switching to screenshare in a sec - walking through the repo, the env vars, and then running a small sample that shows streaming and embeddings.
[00:45] Diego Ramos: One ask from platform - we need to understand VPC options and whether keys can be rotated automatically. Also latency targets - under 120ms for our chat use case.
[00:58] Priya Rao: We'll cover rotation in the KMS section, and Liam will call out the batching knobs that impact latency vs cost.
[01:10] Liam Chen: Ok sharing. (screen noises) Repo layout: /python, /typescript, sample prompt sets. The quickstart script uses REDWOOD_API_KEY env and a .redwoodrc for app-level config. For GCP we show Workload Identity example - pretty small patch to auth code.
[01:35] Eli Zhao: Is that the same as GCP workload identity federation? We use that already for other services.
[01:42] Liam Chen: Yeah same. In our docs it's 'workload-identity' sample. Heads up transcription might show 'workload identity' as two words, sometimes shows as 'world load' in auto transcript.
[01:55] Nora Patel: For prod we likely need SSO and RBAC - can you map how those fit with Redwood's Console?
[02:04] Ava Martinez: Absolutely - Console supports SAML and OIDC for SSO, plus RBAC at token and route level. We'll include our RBAC example for your org structure.
[02:15] Samir Khan: On encryption: we want envelope encryption using our KMS (Cloud KMS) and rotate keys every 90 days. HSM? We might need FIPS level.
[02:27] Liam Chen: Redwood supports bring-your-own-KMS via cloud provider integrations, and we have options to use an HSM-backed key. For rotation, we can automate rewrap operations; I'll send the integration notes. Small caveat: some on-prem setups require Private (VPC) deployment.
[02:45] Nora Patel: What's the difference in cost/latency between Hosted and Dedicated? We want predictable p95 under 200ms.
[02:53] Priya Rao: Hosted is easiest for quickstarts and pilot; Dedicated gives isolation and reserved throughput which helps p95 predictability. There's also Private/VPC for air-gapped needs. We'll provide a cost/latency tradeoff doc.
[03:10] Liam Chen: Now running the Python quickstart: pip install redwood-inference-client, export REDWOOD_API_KEY and REDWOOD_ENV=staging-sf-sandbox, then python examples/chat_quickstart.py.
[03:30] [screen share typing sounds]
[03:38] Liam Chen: Example output - streaming tokens, you can see the latency on the console. Alert: sample uses a small model variant, for volume you'll want a quantized model and batching.
[04:01] Diego Ramos: How does batching affect session latency? We have interactive chat so can't batch too long.
[04:10] Liam Chen: Right - continuous batching groups requests in the background; you can control max_wait_ms and batch_size. For low-latency interactive chat, set max_wait_ms low (15-30 ms) and small batch_size. That increases cost slightly.
[04:29] Nora Patel: Does Redwood provide built-in prefix or KV caching?
[04:34] Priya Rao: Yes, we have KV cache support to store past conversation context and prefix caching which can reduce tokens sent to model and save cost. It's configurable per-route in Console.
[04:50] Eli Zhao: Show us the TypeScript example.
[04:56] Liam Chen: Switching to TS folder: npm i @redwood/inference, then sample code: const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY, env: process.env.REDWOOD_ENV }); there's also an async stream API that we demo. 
[05:18] [small crosstalk]
[05:22] Nora Patel: When we run the sandbox what isolation do we get - logs, telemetry? Data never leaves region?
[05:31] Ava Martinez: Sandbox is hosted in a specified region; telemetry and logs are visible in the Console. For data residency you can choose region and for stricter needs Private deployment keeps data in your VPC.
[05:45] Samir Khan: We also need audit logs that feed into our SIEM. Is there a push option?
[05:51] Liam Chen: We export audit logs to S3/Cloud Storage and can stream to your SIEM via syslog or pub/sub. We'll include the audit log retention and export doc.
[06:08] Nora Patel: Could you show a simple KMS integration flow?
[06:12] Liam Chen: Sure — here's the flow: 1) Customer registers KMS key in Console; 2) Redwood encrypts model payload keys with your KMS (envelope encryption); 3) We store wrapped keys; 4) On inference, Redwood requests a decrypt call to KMS. If you require HSM, we route through HSM provider.
[06:40] Samir Khan: That decrypt call latency - will it add to our p95?
[06:45] Liam Chen: Good question. We use cached wrapped keys and a short-lived unwrapped memo so KMS calls are infrequent; the first access may add overhead, but usually negligible if you use caching. We'll include recommended TTLs.
[07:05] Diego Ramos: Any examples of rotatable keys?
[07:09] Liam Chen: Yes - our docs have a rotate-key endpoint and an atomic swap workflow; we'll share the runbook.
[07:20] [10 min of the demo elided for brevity - environment variables, quickstart scripts run, small benchmark run results shown on screen]
[17:30] Nora Patel: We saw the small benchmark - what's the expected token cost for our 2k prompt+response?
[17:37] Priya Rao: We'll produce a cost estimate using your prompt set as an action item - ballpark depends on model size and quantization. We'll do a few model variants.
[17:48] Eli Zhao: On the SDK - can we rotate API keys without downtime?
[17:52] Ava Martinez: Yes, you can create a new key and update envs; we recommend short-lived tokens and automated rotation in CI. We'll attach example CI pipeline snippet.
[18:10] Samir Khan: We've got a security questionnaire, sending it tonight. We'll need SOC2 and ISO docs.
[18:16] Priya Rao: We'll share SOC2 report and compliance pack; note that Private deployments have additional SLAs and on-prem audit capabilities.
[18:28] Diego Ramos: Could you explain model fallbacks? If a region has partial capacity, do you failover?
[18:35] Liam Chen: Smart routing lets you set fallback models or route to another region. We do automated retries and can route to cheaper model if higher-grade model is unavailable. You define policies per-route.
[18:50] Nora Patel: For the pilot, we want to try hosted sandbox with two routes: low-latency chat and batch embeddings. Any best practice?
[18:58] Liam Chen: Yes - isolate routes, enable KV cache for chat, and configure separate batching profiles. We'll share a starter config.
[19:10] Ava Martinez: I'll summarize next steps at the end but quick Q: any blockers to starting the sandbox?
[19:16] Nora Patel: Just internal signoff and the security questionnaire. Also need KMS confirmation.
[19:22] Ava Martinez: Great. We'll provision the sandbox after the questionnaire and send quickstart link.
[19:28] [multiple participants speaking softly about scheduling]
[19:40] Priya Rao: Micro tip - if you want to lower unit cost without hurting latency much, try 4-bit quantized models with small cache sizes. We'll include tuned profiles we use for chat workloads.
[20:00] Samir Khan: Are there examples of rollout/canary policies? We want to roll a model change to 10% traffic first.
[20:06] Liam Chen: Console supports canary/A-B and automatic fallback thresholding. We'll send a sample rollout config.
[20:18] Diego Ramos: Two quick infra questions: how do we manage secrets in CI and is there a recommended key rotation cadence?
[20:25] Ava Martinez: We recommend platform-managed secrets (eg GCP Secret Manager) and short-lived tokens. Rotation cadence depends on risk but 30-90 days is common; KMS rotation as Samir said 90 days is fine.
[20:40] [roughly 30 minutes of more hands-on steps and logs omitted - transcript picks back up at 44:20]
[44:20] Liam Chen: Back to the playbook: I'm running the embedding job now to show bulk throughput - note the batch size and concurrency settings in the job config.
[44:38] Eli Zhao: Throughput looks good. Wanted to confirm data retention settings for embeddings - do you persist raw inputs?
[44:47] Priya Rao: You can configure retention per-route. For pilot we can set zero retention and only store hashed metadata. We'll include default retention policies in the docs.
[45:05] Nora Patel: Any tricky gotchas for our infra team?
[45:10] Liam Chen: Watch out for env mixing between sandbox and prod - use distinct REDWOOD_ENV and RBAC tokens. Also consider region pinning to avoid cross-region egress.
[45:25] Samir Khan: Can Redwood sign the data processing addendum?
[45:29] Ava Martinez: Yes, we'll run legal through the DPA and include SSO and KMS clauses. I'll loop in our legal.
[45:40] Nora Patel: Ok let's talk timeline. If we start the pilot this week, what do you need from us?
[45:45] Ava Martinez: Sandbox owners and the security questionnaire responses. We will provision within 48 hours of receiving the questionnaire. 
[46:00] Diego Ramos: How do we measure success - what metrics should we report?
[46:05] Priya Rao: Latency p50/p95, token cost per request, error rate, and regression on quality (we can hook into your evals). We'll help define a short evaluation plan.
[46:20] Nora Patel: Perfect. Anything else?
[46:23] Ava Martinez: We'll recap action items and next steps in an email and attach the quickstart repo link and benchmark sheet.
[46:33] Liam Chen: I'll follow up with the KMS runbook and the rotate-key example.
[46:40] Samir Khan: We'll fill out the security questionnaire tonight. Expect the first pass by EOD tomorrow.
[46:47] [participants exchange thank-yous]
[46:52] Ava Martinez: Thanks everyone. We'll send the invite for the deep dive next week if needed.
[46:58] Nora Patel: Thanks all, that was great.
[47:02] Meeting ends.

Notes on transcript quality: occasional mishearings (K V cache, 'workload' sometimes miswritten), but all key technical items captured.
